Environmental-reuse values may shift slowly and still leave a durable segment. Requiring never-shift preferences invents an absolute freeze rule for usefulness.

So the statement is False.

title: Uniform Promotion in Mass Marketing
context: Analyze how mass marketing promotes a product to all segments in almost the same way. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Niche marketing to buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer.
Mass marketing to a coastal region and neighbouring inland towns requires a different product formula for every neighbourhood street.
Targeting occasional users rather than intensive daily operators means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging its attractiveness against segmentation criteria.
Positioning toward buyers unwilling to pay the full price of a brand-new device aims to create a distinct image of which product best serves that attitude-based subgroup.
Producing millions of identical units for an Austrian city and its surrounding commuter area can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale.
tactical_explanations:
Niche marketing to price-sensitive device buyers concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose preferences justify a focused offer. Narrow depth is the niche idea.

So the statement is True.

Mass marketing to coastal and inland towns uses one product approach, not a different formula per street. Street-level customisation contradicts mass marketing.

So the statement is False.

Targeting occasional rather than intensive daily operators means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging attractiveness against measurability, profit, access, and durability. Selection follows evaluation; it is not a raw list of every cluster. Behavioural usage intensity defines who is chosen. The statement describes that targeting step correctly.

So the statement is True.

Positioning toward price-sensitive device buyers builds a distinct image of which product serves that attitude-based subgroup. Mental identity work is positioning.

So the statement is True.

Millions of identical units for an Austrian city-commuter market can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale. Volume spreads shared costs across output.

So the statement is True.

title: Mass Marketing for Everyday Products
context: Consider a regional bakery chain that groups customers by city and surrounding commuter towns when planning delivery routes and store openings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Niche marketing to customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods means selling one identical product to the entire national market.
A firm with strategic fit serving adult men and women of all ages should concentrate resources on that segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage.
Grouping buyers in a coastal region and neighbouring inland towns illustrates geographic segmentation because location defines the subgroup.
Describing customers as employed wage earners and retired pensioners illustrates demographic segmentation using measurable population characteristics.
Targeting customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods reflects psychographic segmentation based on attitudes and preferences rather than location alone.
tactical_explanations:
Niche marketing to environmental-reuse buyers focuses on a narrow subgroup, not on one identical product for the entire nation. National sameness is mass marketing.

So the statement is False.

Strategic fit with adult men and women of all ages calls for concentrating resources on that demographic segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage. Focus follows fit.

So the statement is True.

Coastal regions and neighbouring inland towns are grouped by location. That place definition is geographic segmentation. Buyers share a spatial frame rather than an income or lifestyle frame in this cut. Neighbouring inland towns still belong under geography when the link is place. The statement therefore illustrates geographic segmentation correctly for those areas.

So the statement is True.

Employed wage earners and retired pensioners are demographic descriptors based on measurable population characteristics. Employment and retirement status fit that demographic cut.

So the statement is True.

Valuing environmental reuse of second-hand goods is an attitude-based psychographic cut, not a location-only grouping. Preferences define the segment in this example.

So the statement is True.

title: Economies of Scale in Production
context: Analyze economies of scale arising when large identical output spreads some costs across more units. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Distinguishing seasonal purchasers rather than year-round repeat buyers is behavioural segmentation because purchase and usage patterns differ within the product category.
Segment marketing to employed wage earners and retired pensioners means ignoring subgroup differences and promoting one undifferentiated offer.
A segment defined for a coastal region and neighbouring inland towns is measurable when survey and sales data reveal its size and average purchasing power.
Positioning toward seasonal purchasers rather than year-round repeat buyers is unnecessary if the firm already completed geographic segmentation.
Targeting seasonal purchasers rather than year-round repeat buyers means listing every possible subgroup without evaluating attractiveness.
tactical_explanations:
Seasonal purchasers versus year-round repeat buyers differ in purchase timing and usage patterns. That difference is behavioural segmentation inside the product category.

So the statement is True.

Segment marketing differentiates for employed wage earners and retired pensioners. Ignoring differences and promoting one undifferentiated offer is mass marketing, not segment marketing.

So the statement is False.

Survey and sales figures can reveal size and average purchasing power for a coastal-inland segment. Those estimates make the geographic group measurable without a census of every resident. Measurability rests on workable sample or sales data, not exhaustive interviews of every household. The statement ties data to measurability correctly for that place-based group.

So the statement is True.

Positioning toward seasonal purchasers remains necessary after geographic work because the firm still needs an image for that behavioural subgroup. Geography alone does not finish positioning.

So the statement is False.

Targeting seasonal buyers means selecting after attractiveness checks, not listing every subgroup without evaluation. Listing without judgment is not targeting as defined here.

So the statement is False.

title: Cost Per Unit and Total Output
context: Review how mass marketing can reduce cost per unit through increased total output. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Economies of scale for a niche offer to customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods are identical to those for undifferentiated mass production.
A segment of employed wage earners and retired pensioners is profitable only if expected revenue from serving them exceeds the cost of tailored offers.
A firm serving employed wage earners and retired pensioners with strategic fit should spread resources evenly across every segment in the economy.
Producing a tiny customised batch for customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods always yields lower unit cost than mass production of identical units.
A segment of customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods is accessible when advertising and retail channels can reach those customers effectively.
tactical_explanations:
Niche offers for environmental-reuse buyers typically lack the volume of undifferentiated mass production, so scale economies are not identical. Equating them is false.

So the statement is False.

Employed wage earners and retired pensioners form a profitable segment only when expected revenue exceeds tailored-offer costs. Net return, not mere naming, decides profitability.

So the statement is True.

Strategic fit with employed and retired groups calls for concentrating resources on that demographic segment. Spreading evenly across every segment in the economy would dilute the fit advantage. Focus is the point of selecting a strategically matching cluster. The even-spread claim therefore contradicts segment strategy.

So the statement is False.

Tiny customised batches for environmental-reuse buyers do not always beat mass unit costs. Mass identical runs usually enjoy lower unit cost from scale advantages.

So the statement is False.

Environmental-reuse buyers are accessible when advertising and retail channels reach them effectively. Reach through communication and distribution is the accessibility test.

So the statement is True.

title: Mass Marketing Inflexibility
context: Analyze the inflexibility of mass marketing when particular target markets change. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A segment of seasonal purchasers rather than year-round repeat buyers is durable when usage patterns remain stable enough to justify product and promotion planning.
Grouping buyers by self-employed professionals and salaried staff alone is geographic segmentation because demographics describe place.
Mass marketing of a universal staple to a coastal region and neighbouring inland towns and other areas uses one offer promoted in almost the same way everywhere.
Segment marketing to employed wage earners and retired pensioners would offer differentiated products matching the subgroup's identified needs rather than one identical item.
Niche marketing to customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer.
tactical_explanations:
Seasonal versus year-round purchase patterns can be durable when they stay stable enough for product and promotion planning. Relative steadiness supports investment in the offer.

So the statement is True.

Self-employed professionals and salaried staff are demographic groups. Demographics are people traits, not place, so calling that cut geographic mislabels it.

So the statement is False.

Mass marketing of a universal staple across a coastal region, inland towns, and other areas uses one offer promoted almost the same way everywhere. Uniformity across geography is the mass approach. Local street customisation is not required under that logic. The statement describes that one-offer pattern correctly for a staple product.

So the statement is True.

Segment marketing to employed and retired groups would differentiate products to match needs rather than one identical item. Differentiation defines segment marketing in this case.

So the statement is True.

Niche marketing to environmental-reuse buyers concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer. Narrow depth is niche practice here.

So the statement is True.

title: Segment Marketing Differentiation
context: Consider a national soap manufacturer producing millions of identical bars to spread fixed factory costs across a very large output. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Targeting seasonal purchasers rather than year-round repeat buyers means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging its attractiveness against segmentation criteria.
Positioning toward customers who value environmental reuse of second-hand goods aims to create a distinct image of which product best serves that attitude-based subgroup.
Producing millions of identical units for a coastal region and neighbouring inland towns can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale.
A firm with strategic fit serving employed wage earners and retired pensioners should concentrate resources on that segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage.
Grouping buyers in a capital district and peripheral suburbs illustrates geographic segmentation because location defines the subgroup.
tactical_explanations:
Targeting seasonal rather than year-round buyers selects that behavioural subgroup after judging attractiveness against segmentation criteria. Evaluation precedes selection.

So the statement is True.

Positioning toward environmental-reuse buyers builds a distinct image of which product serves that attitude-based subgroup. Identity in the target's mind is positioning.

So the statement is True.

Producing millions of identical units for coastal and inland towns spreads fixed factory costs across high volume. That spreading supports economies of scale when the offer stays undifferentiated. Shared costs fall per unit as identical output rises. The statement links volume production to scale correctly for that geography.

So the statement is True.

Strategic fit with employed wage earners and retired pensioners should concentrate resources on that segment rather than mass coverage of everyone. Focus follows fit.

So the statement is True.

A capital district and peripheral suburbs form a geographic segment because location defines the subgroup. Place, not income, is the grouping key in this cut.

So the statement is True.

title: Strategic Fit in Segment Marketing
context: Analyze how segment marketing focuses limited resources on segments with strategic fit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Describing customers as self-employed professionals and salaried staff illustrates demographic segmentation using measurable population characteristics.
Grouping buyers in a capital district and peripheral suburbs is psychographic segmentation because location reflects personal values.
Targeting users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment reflects psychographic segmentation based on attitudes and preferences rather than location alone.
Distinguishing light users of software licences rather than power users is behavioural segmentation because purchase and usage patterns differ within the product category.
A segment defined for a capital district and peripheral suburbs is measurable when survey and sales data reveal its size and average purchasing power.
tactical_explanations:
Self-employed professionals and salaried staff are demographic descriptors using measurable population characteristics. Employment status fits that demographic cut.

So the statement is True.

Capital districts and peripheral suburbs are geographic location groups. Psychographics concern values and attitudes, so calling the capital-suburb cut psychographic confuses place with values.

So the statement is False.

Users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment are grouped by service attitude and preference, not by map location alone. That preference stance is psychographic segmentation. Targeting them reflects attitudes toward assisted start-up rather than pure geography. The statement places the cut correctly in the psychographic category.

So the statement is True.

Light versus power users of software licences differ in purchase and usage intensity. That pattern difference is behavioural segmentation within the software category.

So the statement is True.

Survey and sales data can measure size and purchasing power for a capital-suburb segment. Those estimates satisfy measurability for the geographic group described.

So the statement is True.

title: Niche Marketing Focus
context: Review niche marketing as concentrating on particular segments or subgroups within segments. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A segment of self-employed professionals and salaried staff is profitable only if expected revenue from serving them exceeds the cost of tailored offers.
A segment of users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment is accessible when advertising and retail channels can reach those customers effectively.
Targeting users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment is behavioural segmentation because attitudes are the same as purchase frequency.
A segment of light users of software licences rather than power users is durable when usage patterns remain stable enough to justify product and promotion planning.
Mass marketing of a universal staple to a capital district and peripheral suburbs and other areas uses one offer promoted in almost the same way everywhere.
tactical_explanations:
Self-employed and salaried segments are profitable only when expected revenue exceeds the cost of tailored offers. Naming the group does not settle the profit test.

So the statement is True.

Hands-on-help users are accessible when advertising and retail channels reach them effectively. Communication and distribution reach define accessibility for this subgroup.

So the statement is True.

Wanting hands-on help when starting equipment is an attitude or preference about service style, which is psychographic. Behavioural segmentation tracks purchase frequency and usage intensity, not that service attitude. Equating attitudes with purchase frequency collapses two bases. The statement therefore mislabels the cut as behavioural.

So the statement is False.

Light versus power software users form a durable behavioural segment when usage stays stable enough for product and promotion plans. Relative steadiness supports planning.

So the statement is True.

Mass marketing a universal staple across a capital district, suburbs, and other areas uses one offer promoted almost the same way everywhere. Uniform promotion is mass logic.

So the statement is True.

title: Small Business Niche Preference
context: Analyze why many small businesses favour niche marketing over mass-market volume. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Segment marketing to self-employed professionals and salaried staff would offer differentiated products matching the subgroup's identified needs rather than one identical item.
Distinguishing light users of software licences rather than power users is demographic segmentation because usage is a social characteristic like age.
Niche marketing to users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer.
A segment of a capital district and peripheral suburbs is automatically profitable whenever it can be named on a map.
Targeting light users of software licences rather than power users means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging its attractiveness against segmentation criteria.
tactical_explanations:
Segment marketing to self-employed and salaried staff offers differentiated products matching subgroup needs rather than one identical item. Differentiation is the segment approach.

So the statement is True.

Light versus power software use is behavioural, based on usage intensity. Demographics cover age, income, and similar social traits; usage is not demographic like age.

So the statement is False.

Niche marketing to users wanting hands-on start-up help concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer. Depth into that service-attitude niche differs from covering every buyer with one mass product. Specialisation matches the narrow preference set. The statement describes niche concentration correctly.

So the statement is True.

Naming a capital district and suburbs on a map does not prove automatic profitability. Revenue must still exceed serving costs for the geographic segment.

So the statement is False.

Targeting light software users means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging attractiveness against segmentation criteria. Selection follows evaluation of the cluster.

So the statement is True.

title: More Segmentation in Niche Marketing
context: Consider a supermarket group analysing age, employment status, and household income before designing loyalty offers for different shopper profiles. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A segment of self-employed professionals and salaried staff is accessible whenever it is measurable, even if no channel reaches them.
Positioning toward users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment aims to create a distinct image of which product best serves that attitude-based subgroup.
A segment of users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment is durable only if preferences never shift, making short-term trends irrelevant.
Producing millions of identical units for a capital district and peripheral suburbs can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale.
A firm with strategic fit serving self-employed professionals and salaried staff should concentrate resources on that segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage.
tactical_explanations:
Measurability of self-employed and salaried groups does not create accessibility if no channel reaches them. Reach and measurement remain separate criteria for usefulness.

So the statement is False.

Positioning toward hands-on-help users creates a distinct image of which product serves that attitude-based subgroup. Mental identity for the niche is positioning work.

So the statement is True.

Durability for hands-on-help preferences requires only enough stability for planning, not a forever freeze that makes short-term trends irrelevant by definition. Preferences may drift slowly without destroying the segment. Absolute never-shift rules invent an impossible test. The statement's only-if-never-shift claim is therefore false.

So the statement is False.

Millions of identical units for a capital-suburb geography can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale. Volume spreads shared costs across identical output.

So the statement is True.

Strategic fit with self-employed and salaried staff should concentrate resources on that segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage. Focus follows fit for the firm.

So the statement is True.

title: Target Market Definition
context: Analyze a target market as the group toward whom a business markets with a tailored strategy. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Grouping buyers in a mountain province and valley municipalities illustrates geographic segmentation because location defines the subgroup.
Describing customers as households grouped by declared income brackets illustrates demographic segmentation using measurable population characteristics.
Mass marketing to a capital district and peripheral suburbs requires a different product formula for every neighbourhood street.
Targeting shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty reflects psychographic segmentation based on attitudes and preferences rather than location alone.
Niche marketing to users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment means selling one identical product to the entire national market.
tactical_explanations:
Mountain provinces and valley municipalities are grouped by location. That place definition illustrates geographic segmentation for those regional buyers.

So the statement is True.

Households grouped by declared income brackets are a demographic cut using measurable population characteristics. Income levels fit demographic segmentation as taught.

So the statement is True.

Mass marketing to a capital district and suburbs uses one offer, not a different product formula for every neighbourhood street. Street-level customisation contradicts the mass approach. Uniformity across the area is the mass rule for staples. The statement's every-street requirement invents a false mass condition that the chapter never teaches.

So the statement is False.

Shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty are grouped by attitude and preference. That psychographic cut is not location alone for the targeting decision.

So the statement is True.

Niche marketing to hands-on-help users focuses on a narrow subgroup, not on one identical product for the entire national market. National sameness is mass marketing.

So the statement is False.

title: Satisfying Target Market Needs
context: Review how a target market strategy aims to satisfy specific needs and preferences. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Distinguishing infrequent maintainers rather than continuous heavy consumers is behavioural segmentation because purchase and usage patterns differ within the product category.
A segment defined for a mountain province and valley municipalities is measurable when survey and sales data reveal its size and average purchasing power.
Segment marketing to self-employed professionals and salaried staff means ignoring subgroup differences and promoting one undifferentiated offer.
Positioning toward light users of software licences rather than power users is unnecessary if the firm already completed geographic segmentation.
A segment of households grouped by declared income brackets is profitable only if expected revenue from serving them exceeds the cost of tailored offers.
tactical_explanations:
Infrequent maintainers versus continuous heavy consumers differ in purchase and usage patterns. That intensity difference is behavioural segmentation in the category.

So the statement is True.

Mountain-province and valley segments are measurable when survey and sales data reveal size and average purchasing power. Estimates satisfy measurability without full interviews.

So the statement is True.

Segment marketing to self-employed and salaried staff differentiates offers for those subgroups. Ignoring differences and promoting one undifferentiated item is mass marketing. The statement swaps the segment label onto a mass practice. Differentiation by needs, not sameness of offer, defines segment marketing here for those employment groups.

So the statement is False.

Positioning toward light software users remains necessary after geographic segmentation because image still must be set for that behavioural subgroup. Geography alone does not finish positioning.

So the statement is False.

Income-bracket households are profitable only when expected revenue exceeds tailored-offer costs. Net return decides the profit criterion for that demographic group.

So the statement is True.

title: Targeting as First Strategy Step
context: Analyze targeting as the first step toward an effective marketing strategy. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A segment of shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty is accessible when advertising and retail channels can reach those customers effectively.
A segment of infrequent maintainers rather than continuous heavy consumers is durable when usage patterns remain stable enough to justify product and promotion planning.
Targeting light users of software licences rather than power users means listing every possible subgroup without evaluating attractiveness.
Economies of scale for a niche offer to users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment are identical to those for undifferentiated mass production.
A firm serving self-employed professionals and salaried staff with strategic fit should spread resources evenly across every segment in the economy.
tactical_explanations:
Reliability-over-novelty shoppers are accessible when advertising and retail channels reach them effectively. Communication and distribution reach define accessibility here.

So the statement is True.

Infrequent maintainers versus heavy consumers form a durable behavioural segment when usage stays stable enough for product and promotion planning. Relative steadiness supports plans.

So the statement is True.

Targeting light software users means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging attractiveness. Listing every possible subgroup without evaluation skips targeting's core step. Attractiveness checks against segmentation criteria come before selection. The statement's list-without-evaluation reading is therefore false.

So the statement is False.

Niche offers for hands-on-help users typically lack mass volume, so scale economies are not identical to undifferentiated mass production. Equating them is wrong.

So the statement is False.

Strategic fit with self-employed and salaried staff calls for concentrated resources, not even spreads across every segment in the economy. Focus follows fit.

So the statement is False.

title: Marketing Mix After Targeting
context: Consider a tutoring service positioning itself as the supportive option for adult learners returning to formal study after years in employment. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mass marketing of a universal staple to a mountain province and valley municipalities and other areas uses one offer promoted in almost the same way everywhere.
Segment marketing to households grouped by declared income brackets would offer differentiated products matching the subgroup's identified needs rather than one identical item.
Niche marketing to shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty concentrates on a narrow subgroup whose specialised preferences justify a focused offer.
Producing a tiny customised batch for users wanting hands-on help when starting equipment always yields lower unit cost than mass production of identical units.
Targeting infrequent maintainers rather than continuous heavy consumers means selecting that behavioural subgroup after judging its attractiveness against segmentation criteria.
tactical_explanations:
Mass marketing a universal staple across mountain provinces, valleys, and other areas uses one offer promoted almost the same way everywhere. Uniform promotion is mass logic.

So the statement is True.

Segment marketing to income-bracket households would differentiate products to match subgroup needs rather than one identical item. Differentiation defines the segment approach.

So the statement is True.

Niche marketing to reliability-over-novelty shoppers concentrates on a narrow preference subgroup whose specialised attitudes justify a focused offer. Depth into that psychographic niche differs from covering every buyer with one mass staple. Specialisation matches the reliability priority. The statement describes niche concentration correctly.

So the statement is True.

Tiny customised batches for hands-on-help users do not always yield lower unit cost than mass identical production. Scale usually favours the mass run on unit cost.

So the statement is False.

Targeting infrequent maintainers selects that behavioural subgroup after judging attractiveness against segmentation criteria. Evaluation precedes selection of the cluster.

So the statement is True.

title: Employed and Retired Demographics
context: Analyze employed and retired adults as demographic characteristics in segmentation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Positioning toward shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty aims to create a distinct image of which product best serves that attitude-based subgroup.
Producing millions of identical units for a mountain province and valley municipalities can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale.
A firm with strategic fit serving households grouped by declared income brackets should concentrate resources on that segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage.
Grouping buyers in a border county and adjacent cross-border shoppers illustrates geographic segmentation because location defines the subgroup.
Describing customers as buyers classified by completed education level illustrates demographic segmentation using measurable population characteristics.
tactical_explanations:
Positioning toward reliability-over-novelty shoppers builds a distinct image of which product serves that attitude-based subgroup. Mental identity work is positioning.

So the statement is True.

Millions of identical units for mountain provinces and valleys can spread fixed factory costs and support economies of scale. Volume spreads shared costs across geography.

So the statement is True.

Strategic fit with income-bracket households should concentrate resources on that demographic segment rather than undifferentiated mass coverage. Focusing where fit is strongest improves the chance that tailored offers pay off. Scattering across every group would dilute that advantage. The statement links fit to resource concentration correctly.

So the statement is True.

Border counties and adjacent cross-border shoppers are grouped by location. That place definition illustrates geographic segmentation for the cross-border trade area.

So the statement is True.

Buyers classified by completed education level form a demographic segment using measurable population characteristics. Education status fits that demographic cut cleanly.

So the statement is True.

title: Self-Employed Demographic Segment
context: Review self-employed status as a demographic variable for customer description. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Targeting clients seeking personalised service rather than self-service reflects psychographic segmentation based on attitudes and preferences rather than location alone.
Distinguishing trial buyers before occasional repeat purchase is behavioural segmentation because purchase and usage patterns differ within the product category.
A segment defined for a border county and adjacent cross-border shoppers is measurable when survey and sales data reveal its size and average purchasing power.
Grouping buyers by households grouped by declared income brackets alone is geographic segmentation because demographics describe place.
A segment of buyers classified by completed education level is profitable only if expected revenue from serving them exceeds the cost of tailored offers.
tactical_explanations:
Clients seeking personalised service rather than self-service are grouped by service attitude. That preference cut is psychographic, not location alone for targeting.

So the statement is True.

Trial buyers before occasional repeat purchase differ in purchase stage and usage pattern. That difference is behavioural segmentation within the product category.

So the statement is True.

Border-county and cross-border shopper segments are measurable when survey and sales data reveal size and average purchasing power. Geographic groups become useful once those estimates exist. Measurability does not require interviewing every cross-border buyer. The statement ties data to the measurable criterion correctly.

So the statement is True.

Income-bracket households are demographic, not geographic. Demographics describe people traits; place describes geography. Mislabeling income groups as geographic confuses the bases.

So the statement is False.

Education-level buyers are profitable only when expected revenue exceeds tailored-offer costs. Net return, not education labels alone, settles profitability for the segment.

So the statement is True.

title: Occasional Use Behavioural Segment
context: Analyze occasional-use buyers as a behavioural segment distinct from heavy users. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Grouping buyers in a mountain province and valley municipalities is psychographic segmentation because location reflects personal values.
Targeting shoppers prioritising reliability over fashionable novelty is behavioural segmentation because attitudes are the same as purchase frequency.
Distinguishing infrequent maintainers rather than continuous heavy consumers is demographic segmentation because usage is a social characteristic like age.
A segment of clients seeking personalised service rather than self-service is accessible when advertising and retail channels can reach those customers effectively.
A segment of a mountain province and valley municipalities is automatically profitable whenever it can be named on a map.
tactical_explanations:
Mountain provinces and valley municipalities are geographic location groups. Psychographics concern values, so calling that place cut psychographic mislabels the basis.

So the statement is False.

Reliability-over-novelty priorities are attitudes, hence psychographic. Behavioural segmentation tracks purchase frequency and usage, not that preference stance. Equating attitudes with frequency collapses two bases.

So the statement is False.

Infrequent maintainers versus continuous heavy consumers differ in usage intensity, which is behavioural. Demographics cover age, income, and similar social traits. Treating usage as demographic like age invents a false category swap. Purchase and usage patterns define the behavioural cut here, not census-style social measures.

So the statement is False.

Personalised-service clients are accessible when advertising and retail channels reach them effectively. Communication and distribution reach define accessibility for that psychographic group.

So the statement is True.

Naming a mountain-valley area on a map does not prove automatic profitability. Revenue must still exceed the cost of serving that geographic segment of buyers.

So the statement is False.

title: Marketing Mix Four Ps Overview
context: Review the marketing mix as a harmonised blend of product, price, place, and promotion tools. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A marketing mix is a harmonised blend of marketing tools that best meets the needs and wants of customers in the targeted market.
The marketing mix consists of only product and promotion because price and place are determined entirely by competitors.
Product is the least important element of the marketing mix because pricing decisions alone determine sales.
Place in the marketing mix refers primarily to the geographic location of the business headquarters.
The marketing mix consists of the four elements product, price, place, and promotion, commonly called the four Ps.
tactical_explanations:
A marketing mix is a harmonised blend of tools that best meets needs and wants in the targeted market. Coordination across tools is the point of the mix.

So the statement is True.

The mix includes product, price, place, and promotion. Price and place are not left entirely to competitors; the firm sets them as mix elements. Dropping those two invents a two-P mix the chapter does not teach.

So the statement is False.

Product is a core mix element; pricing alone does not determine sales. Features, quality, and assortment shape demand alongside price, channels, and messages. Calling product the least important because price alone drives sales invents a false ranking among the tools. All four Ps work together in the chapter's marketing mix overview.

So the statement is False.

Place in the mix means distribution and channel decisions that get the offer to customers, not the geographic address of headquarters. HQ location is not the place-P definition.

So the statement is False.

The four elements product, price, place, and promotion are the classic four Ps of the marketing mix. That list matches the chapter overview of the mix toolkit.

So the statement is True.

title: Harmonised Blend of Marketing Tools
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Promotion in the marketing mix means reducing the list price until stock is cleared from the warehouse.
A product line consists of completely unrelated goods such as laptops and restaurant meals grouped for accounting convenience.
Mix extension adds new variants within one existing line, such as another flavour in the same ice-cream range.
The basic idea of the marketing mix is to provide a good at an affordable price at a convenient place and communicate a message to promote sales.
Decisions across the four Ps of the marketing mix are based on market research findings about the targeted market.
tactical_explanations:
Promotion is the communication side of the mix: advertising, personal selling, sales events, and public relations. Cutting list price to clear warehouse stock is a price decision, not the definition of promotion.

So the statement is False.

A product line groups similar offerings, such as several laptop models that differ only in detail. Laptops and restaurant meals share no product similarity and would not form one line merely for accounting convenience. Relatedness, not ledger grouping, defines a line.

So the statement is False.

Mix extension widens the portfolio by adding an entirely new product line, such as yogurts beside ice cream. Another flavour inside the same ice-cream range deepens one existing line and is therefore line extension. Treating an extra flavour as mix extension swaps width for depth and mislabels the move. The chapter keeps those two expansion routes distinct for a reason. The statement therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

The marketing-mix idea is to offer a suitable good, charge an affordable price, place it where buyers can reach it, and communicate a promotional message that supports sales. That four-part coordination is exactly what the statement summarises.

So the statement is True.

Choices on product, price, place, and promotion draw on market-research findings about the targeted customers. Research anchors those mix decisions rather than leaving them to guesswork alone.

So the statement is True.

title: Product P at the Heart of Marketing
context: Review Figure 15 on the four elements of the marketing mix based on market research. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Line extension widens the product mix by adding an entirely new product line such as yogurts beside ice cream.
A relaunch always requires eliminating the product from the product line and replacing it with a new category.
Minor packaging changes are classified as mix extension because they alter how the product line is presented.
Each of the four Ps comprises several tools that marketers can combine within the overall marketing mix.
Brand loyalty is unrelated to the product element and belongs exclusively to the promotion P of the marketing mix.
tactical_explanations:
Line extension adds variants inside one existing line. Adding an entirely new yogurt line beside ice cream widens mix width and is mix extension, not line extension.

So the statement is False.

A relaunch can refresh packaging, colour, or presentation while the product stays in the line. Elimination and full category replacement are separate contraction or substitution choices, not a required step for every relaunch.

So the statement is False.

Minor packaging changes sit under product-mix alteration as a relaunch. Mix extension means adding a new product line to the portfolio, not restyling how an existing line appears on the shelf. Labelling a packaging tweak as mix extension confuses alteration with width expansion. The chapter's alteration path already covers those surface refreshes. The statement therefore misclassifies the change.

So the statement is False.

Each of the four Ps contains several tools that marketers combine inside the overall mix. Advertising and personal selling under promotion, or discounts under price, illustrate that toolkit structure. The statement describes that layered design correctly.

So the statement is True.

Brand loyalty is built through the product element as recognition and trust around the offer, not only through promotion messages. Placing loyalty exclusively under promotion erases the product-side role of brands.

So the statement is False.

title: Product Lines and Mix Width
context: Analyze the product element of the marketing mix as the first P covering goods and services offered. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Brands consist only of production patents and contain no name, symbol, or sign visible to customers.
A harmonised marketing mix coordinates product, price, place, and promotion rather than treating each P independently.
The four Ps framework helps a business align what it sells, what it charges, where it is sold, and how it is promoted.
Marketing-mix planning seeks to satisfy targeted customers' needs and wants through a coordinated set of tools.
During introduction the product life cycle always shows peak profit because early buyers pay premium prices.
tactical_explanations:
Brands use names, symbols, and signs customers can see and recognise. Patents may protect technology, yet they do not replace the visible brand marks that differentiate products in the market.

So the statement is False.

A harmonised marketing mix coordinates product, price, place, and promotion instead of letting each P drift on its own. Alignment across the four tools is the point of treating them as one mix.

So the statement is True.

The four Ps give managers a checklist for what is sold, what is charged, where buyers can obtain it, and how the offer is promoted. Using that frame keeps those decisions pointed at the same customer target. Without it, price might undercut product quality claims or place might block access while ads promise convenience. Coordination is the practical payoff of the framework. The statement captures that alignment role accurately.

So the statement is True.

Marketing-mix planning aims to satisfy targeted customers' needs and wants by combining the available tools. Customer satisfaction through coordinated decisions is the planning purpose named here.

So the statement is True.

Introduction typically begins with low or negative profit while development and launch costs outweigh early sales. Peak profit belongs later, usually in maturity, not at introduction by default.

So the statement is False.

title: Brands and Product Differentiation
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The product element of the marketing mix refers to all goods and services that are offered by a business.
The decline stage is characterised by the highest sales volume and peak profit in the product life cycle.
Product is at the heart of marketing and represents the most important decision of a business within the four Ps.
Maturity always lasts less than one year before every product automatically enters decline.
A question mark in the BCG matrix has high relative market share and low market growth.
tactical_explanations:
Within the marketing mix, product covers every good and service the business offers. Tangible items and related services sit under that same product P.

So the statement is True.

Decline is the stage of falling sales and shrinking profit as the product nears the end of its cycle. Highest volume and peak profit belong earlier, typically around maturity, not in decline.

So the statement is False.

Product sits at the centre of marketing because without a credible offer the other Ps have nothing solid to price, place, or promote. Managers treat product decisions as the most important mix choice for that reason. Features, range, brand, and life-cycle role all hang on what is being sold. Price and promotion cannot rescue an offer that fails its purpose. Calling product the heart of the mix therefore matches the chapter framing.

So the statement is True.

Maturity length varies widely by category; detergents may linger for years while fads fade quickly. No rule forces every product out of maturity in under one year.

So the statement is False.

A question mark pairs low relative market share with high market growth. High share with low growth describes a cash cow, not a question mark.

So the statement is False.

title: Relaunch Versus Major Alteration
context: Analyze the role of brands in product differentiation, recognition, and loyalty within the product P. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Most businesses offer not just one product but a range of products within their portfolio.
Products that are very similar, such as several slightly different laptop computers, represent a product line.
A business can specialise in just one product line or diversify by offering different product lines such as laptops and monitors.
Increasing the number of different product lines widens the product mix of a business.
A star in the BCG matrix combines low relative market share with low market growth.
tactical_explanations:
Most firms sell a range of products rather than a single item. Portfolios with several offerings are the ordinary business pattern the statement describes.

So the statement is True.

Slightly different laptop models form a product line because the goods are closely related variants. Similarity within that group is what makes them a line rather than unrelated catalogue items.

So the statement is True.

A business may specialise in one product line or diversify across several, such as laptops and monitors sold together. Specialisation keeps mix width narrow; diversification widens it by adding distinct lines. Both strategies are legitimate product-mix choices depending on capability and market aim. The statement correctly allows either path. Breadth of lines, not a single mandatory structure, defines the mix decision.

So the statement is True.

Adding more distinct product lines increases product-mix width. Width measures how many different lines the firm offers, so more lines mean a wider mix.

So the statement is True.

A star combines high relative market share with high market growth. Low share and low growth describe a poor dog, not a star. The BCG cell depends on both axes together.

So the statement is False.

title: Line Extension Within a Product Line
context: Review minor packaging and colour changes as a relaunch within product-mix alteration. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Offering only laptop computers illustrates specialising in a single product line within the product mix.
A cash cow has low relative market share in a rapidly growing market and requires heavy expansion investment.
A poor dog has high relative market share and high market growth and is the most valuable portfolio position.
The BCG matrix plots absolute market share against production cost per unit rather than relative share and growth.
Penetration pricing sets a very high initial price to skim revenue from early adopters only.
tactical_explanations:
Offering only laptop computers means the firm specialises in one product line. That single-line focus illustrates specialisation within the product mix as the statement says.

So the statement is True.

A cash cow holds high relative share in a low-growth market and usually needs less expansion spend. Low share in a rapidly growing market is a question mark, not a cash cow.

So the statement is False.

A poor dog combines low relative market share with low market growth and sits near the least attractive portfolio corner. High share with high growth describes a star, the opposite of a poor dog. Calling the poor dog the most valuable position reverses the BCG ranking. Value concentrates in stars and cash cows, not in weak share and weak growth together. The statement therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

The BCG matrix plots relative market share against market growth. Absolute share versus unit production cost is not the chapter's BCG axes and invents a different diagram.

So the statement is False.

Penetration pricing starts low to win share quickly. A very high initial price aimed at early adopters is price skimming, not penetration pricing.

So the statement is False.

title: Mix Extension Adding New Lines
context: Consider a beverage company using charm pricing on supermarket shelves and trade discounts for large retailers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Services such as technical support and online help count as products within the product element of the marketing mix.
Price skimming means launching with a low price to maximise volume in the first month of sales.
Packaging, labelling, and colour variants can form part of the product decision within the marketing mix.
Cost-plus pricing ignores production costs and sets price only according to competitor advertisements.
A business may offer goods, related services, and tailored software solutions as distinct products in its portfolio.
tactical_explanations:
Technical support and online help are services offered to customers, so they count as products under the product element. Intangible form does not eject them from that P.

So the statement is True.

Price skimming launches high and may later fall as competition rises. Launching low to maximise early volume is penetration pricing. The statement swaps those two strategies.

So the statement is False.

Packaging, labelling, and colour choices shape how the offer appears and are treated as product decisions inside the mix. Those surface attributes still belong to what is sold, not only to advertising copy. A colour refresh or new label can support recognition without changing the core formula. Product managers therefore own packaging variants alongside features and range. The statement places those elements correctly under product.

So the statement is True.

Cost-plus pricing builds selling price from production costs plus a markup. Ignoring costs and copying only competitor ads is not cost-plus logic.

So the statement is False.

Goods, related services, and tailored software can each stand as distinct products in one portfolio. Multiple product types inside one firm are allowed under the product P.

So the statement is True.

title: Product-Mix Expansion Strategies
context: Review product-mix strategies of expansion, alteration, and contraction in Figure 16. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Brands are created to support product differentiation within the product element of the marketing mix.
A brand consists of a name or a few words and/or a symbol and/or a sign that distinguishes a product or business.
Brands are intended to build a USP, brand recognition, and brand loyalty among customers.
Psychological pricing requires every product to be sold at a round number such as €10.00 without exception.
Wholesalers sell products directly to final consumers at retail shops they operate under their own brand only.
tactical_explanations:
Brands exist to differentiate the offer inside the product element. Differentiation through name, symbol, or sign is a core brand purpose in that P.

So the statement is True.

A brand is a name, a few words, and/or a symbol or sign that distinguishes a product or business. That visible identity package is exactly the definition used here.

So the statement is True.

Brands are meant to support a unique selling proposition, make the offer recognisable, and encourage loyalty so customers return. Recognition and trust grow when the mark stays consistent and quality holds. Without those aims, a logo would be decoration rather than a marketing asset. The chapter links brands to USP, recognition, and loyalty for that reason. The statement restates those intentions correctly.

So the statement is True.

Psychological pricing often uses charm endings such as €9.99; it does not require every item to sell at a round €10.00. Forcing round numbers alone misstates the tool.

So the statement is False.

Wholesalers typically sell in bulk to retailers, not only as branded retail shops selling straight to final consumers. The statement invents a wholesaler role the chapter does not require.

So the statement is False.

title: Product-Mix Alteration and Contraction
context: Analyze the product life cycle model of introduction, growth, maturity, and decline stages. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Some brands look the same worldwide with consistent colour and font to maintain global recognition.
Brands serve as a guarantee of stable quality and a maintained level of quality across markets.
Brands can render trust and safety of choice for customers who seek familiar products abroad.
Brand loyalty encourages customers to repurchase products associated with a trusted name or symbol.
A recognisable brand symbol can reinforce the USP communicated through the wider marketing mix.
tactical_explanations:
Some brands keep the same look worldwide, including colour and font, so recognition travels with travellers and across markets. Consistency supports that global familiarity. Local tweaks may exist, yet many marks stay visually stable on purpose. Worldwide sameness of key brand cues is therefore a real branding practice. The statement describes that pattern accurately.

So the statement is True.

Brands can signal a stable quality level customers expect to find again. That quality guarantee function helps buyers choose with less uncertainty across purchases.

So the statement is True.

Familiar brands can make choice feel safer when customers buy abroad, because the mark signals known quality and trust. Trust and safety of choice are brand benefits named here.

So the statement is True.

Brand loyalty pushes customers to repurchase products tied to a trusted name or symbol. Repeat buying is the loyalty outcome the statement describes.

So the statement is True.

A recognisable brand symbol can reinforce the USP carried through the wider marketing mix. Symbol and message work together rather than in isolation.

So the statement is True.

title: Introduction Stage of Product Life Cycle
context: Consider a book publisher selling through bookshops, online platforms, and direct school supply contracts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retailers purchase products in bulk from producers and resell exclusively to other wholesalers downstream.
Minor changes such as different packaging or colours are called a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
When a relaunch is not enough to keep customers satisfied, major changes or elimination from the line may be necessary.
Adding new products to an existing product line is a line extension, such as producing more flavours of ice cream.
Direct distribution always requires at least two intermediaries between producer and customer.
tactical_explanations:
Retailers buy to sell to end customers at shops or other points of sale. Reselling exclusively to other wholesalers describes a wholesaler-to-wholesaler path, not the retailer role.

So the statement is False.

Minor packaging or colour changes are called a relaunch under product-mix alteration. The core product stays, while presentation is refreshed to regain attention. That limited change is distinct from eliminating the item or adding a whole new line. Managers use relaunch when a light refresh may restore appeal. The statement classifies those minor changes correctly.

So the statement is True.

When a relaunch fails to satisfy customers, major redesign or elimination from the line may follow. Escalation beyond a light refresh is part of alteration and contraction logic.

So the statement is True.

Line extension adds new products inside an existing line, such as more ice-cream flavours. Depth increases while the line identity remains. That is the move the statement names.

So the statement is True.

Direct distribution reaches customers without intermediaries. Requiring at least two intermediaries describes an indirect path, the opposite of direct.

So the statement is False.

title: Growth Stage Sales and Profit Patterns
context: Analyze the Boston Consulting Group matrix using relative market share and market growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Adding a new product line to the portfolio is a mix extension, such as yogurts in addition to ice cream.
Line extension increases the depth of a product line by adding variants within that line.
Indirect distribution means the producer delivers every product personally to each household without any retailer.
Online sales channels belong to the promotion P because they only advertise products without enabling purchase.
Mix extension increases the number of product lines offered by the business.
tactical_explanations:
Adding yogurts beside an ice-cream range introduces a new product line and is therefore mix extension. Portfolio width rises when that second line appears.

So the statement is True.

Line extension deepens one product line by adding variants within it. Extra flavours or versions increase depth without creating a separate line. The statement states that depth effect correctly.

So the statement is True.

Indirect distribution relies on intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers. Personal delivery by the producer to every household with no retailer is direct distribution, or at least not the indirect pattern. The statement reverses the channel logic by treating producer-only delivery as indirect. Intermediaries are the defining feature of the indirect path. The claim therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Online sales channels let customers buy, so they belong to place as access and distribution, not only to promotion as advertising. Enabling purchase keeps them inside place decisions.

So the statement is False.

Mix extension raises the number of product lines the business offers. More lines mean a wider mix under that expansion route, not merely deeper variants.

So the statement is True.

title: Maturity Stage Profit Peak
context: Review BCG categories of stars, question marks, cash cows, and poor dogs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Personal selling is a price tool because sales staff negotiate discounts that permanently replace promotion.
Product-mix expansion can occur through line extension or mix extension strategies.
Advertising is classified under place because it determines which warehouse stores the finished goods.
Altering existing products over time creates a new range instead of the previous one within alteration strategy.
Public relations is a product-mix contraction strategy that eliminates underperforming brands from the portfolio.
tactical_explanations:
Personal selling is a promotion tool: sales staff communicate and persuade. Negotiated discounts may use price levers, yet that does not reclassify personal selling as a permanent price tool that replaces promotion.

So the statement is False.

Product-mix expansion proceeds through line extension or mix extension. Those two routes deepen a line or add new lines. The statement names both expansion strategies correctly.

So the statement is True.

Advertising informs and persuades as a promotion tool; it does not decide which warehouse holds finished goods. Warehouse storage sits under place and operations, not under advertising classification. Calling advertising a place tool because of storage invents a false link. Message design and media choice remain promotional work. The statement therefore misplaces advertising in the mix.

So the statement is False.

Alteration changes existing products over time so a new range replaces the previous one. That refreshed set is the alteration outcome described here.

So the statement is True.

Public relations builds a favourable image as a promotion activity. Eliminating weak brands is product-mix contraction, not public relations. The statement confuses image work with portfolio pruning.

So the statement is False.

title: Decline Stage Falling Sales
context: Consider a furniture retailer combining showroom display, home-delivery logistics, and finance instalment offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Economies of scale in the growth stage always raise average unit costs as output increases.
Eliminating products or whole lines from the range reflects contraction within the product-mix strategy.
Cash cows receive the highest promotional investment because market growth in their segment remains rapid.
Stars no longer require promotional or production investment once they first achieve high market share.
A business may eliminate a product from its range when a relaunch does not seem promising.
tactical_explanations:
Economies of scale in growth typically lower average unit costs as output rises, not raise them. Higher volume spreads fixed costs and can improve efficiency. Claiming costs always rise with growth output reverses that usual pattern. Falling average costs help explain why profit often improves in growth. The absolute upward-cost claim therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Removing products or whole lines from the range is contraction within product-mix strategy. Portfolio pruning is exactly that contraction move.

So the statement is True.

Cash cows sit in low-growth markets and usually receive lower promotional investment while revenues stay strong. Highest promotion in rapidly growing segments fits stars or question marks better than cash cows.

So the statement is False.

Stars still need promotional and production investment to defend a strong position in a growing market. First reaching high share does not end the need to invest.

So the statement is False.

When a relaunch looks unpromising, the firm may eliminate the product from its range. Elimination after a weak relaunch prospect is a recognised contraction choice.

So the statement is True.

title: BCG Matrix Relative Share and Growth
context: Review how stars combine strong market share with continued market growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Product-mix strategies include expansion, alteration, and contraction as shown in the textbook framework.
Product-mix contraction means adding new flavours within an existing ice-cream line to increase depth.
Specialising in one sort of product by offering just one product line narrows the product-mix width.
Diversifying production by offering different product lines increases the width of the product mix.
Increasing product-mix width means adding more variants within the same single product line only.
tactical_explanations:
Product-mix strategies cover expansion, alteration, and contraction in the textbook framework. Those three routes organise how the portfolio grows, changes, or shrinks.

So the statement is True.

Product-mix contraction removes products or lines from the range. Adding new flavours inside an ice-cream line deepens that line and is line extension, an expansion move. Labelling flavour additions as contraction reverses the direction of change. Depth increases when variants arrive; contraction would cut offerings instead. The statement therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Specialising in one product line narrows product-mix width. Width stays small when only one sort of product is offered across the portfolio.

So the statement is True.

Diversifying across different product lines increases mix width. More distinct lines widen the portfolio under that diversification path as intended.

So the statement is True.

Increasing mix width means adding different product lines, not only more variants inside one line. Variants within one line raise depth, not width.

So the statement is False.

title: Question Marks in Growing Markets
context: Analyze cash cows as high-share products in markets with low growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Specialising in one product line diversifies the product mix by increasing the number of different lines offered.
A harmonised marketing mix can ignore customer needs in the targeted market if promotion spending is high enough.
Market research informs only the product P and has no role in price, place, or promotion decisions.
The product life cycle is a theoretical model of stages over a product's life span that differ in sales volume and profit.
Fad products typically remain in maturity for decades like detergents and toothpaste before any decline occurs.
tactical_explanations:
Specialising in one product line keeps the mix narrow; it does not diversify by adding different lines. Diversification requires more lines, the opposite of single-line focus.

So the statement is False.

A harmonised mix still rests on customer needs in the targeted market. Heavy promotion cannot justify ignoring those needs. Research-based customer fit remains required.

So the statement is False.

Market research informs price, place, and promotion as well as product. Channel design, message content, and pricing levels all draw on what research finds about the target. Claiming research touches only product would leave the other Ps unguided. The chapter ties mix decisions generally to research findings. The narrow product-only claim is therefore false.

So the statement is False.

The product life cycle is a theoretical model of stages across a product's life that differ in sales volume and profit. Introduction, growth, maturity, and decline are those stages. The statement states that model role correctly.

So the statement is True.

Fad products often leave the market quickly, sometimes within a year. Detergents and toothpaste illustrate long maturity, not fad-like decades of maturity for fads themselves.

So the statement is False.

title: Stars and Strong Market Position
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Detergents and toothpaste are cited as examples of products with very short fad-like life cycles under one year.
Before market introduction there are no sales, yet product development costs mean the introduction phase starts with a loss.
After product launch, introductory prices may be low and heavy promotion may keep costs above sales early in introduction.
Towards the end of the introduction phase, revenues can exceed costs and a small profit may emerge.
During the growth period, sales increase more rapidly than costs and average costs may fall due to economies of scale.
tactical_explanations:
Detergents and toothpaste are textbook examples of long or seemingly indefinite maturity, not of fad cycles under one year. Short fad timing belongs to other categories.

So the statement is False.

Before launch there are no sales, yet development costs already exist, so introduction begins in loss. Cost without revenue is the early introduction pattern the statement names.

So the statement is True.

After launch, low introductory prices and heavy promotion can keep costs above sales for a stretch of the introduction stage. Awareness spending and trial discounts raise outflows while volume is still thin. That early imbalance is why introduction often shows loss even after the product is on the market. Managers expect the gap to narrow only toward the end of the phase. The statement links low prices and heavy promotion to costs exceeding sales correctly.

So the statement is True.

Toward the end of introduction, revenues may finally exceed costs and a small profit can appear. That late-introduction turn toward profit is a recognised possibility.

So the statement is True.

In growth, sales rise faster than costs and average costs may fall through economies of scale. Rapid volume with improving cost positions is the growth pattern described here.

So the statement is True.

title: Cash Cows in Low-Growth Markets
context: Analyze the price element of the marketing mix as the amount customers pay for the offering. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Adding yogurts beside an ice-cream line is classified as line extension rather than mix extension in the marketing-mix framework.
Business profit usually rises during the growth stage and peaks in the maturity stage of the product life cycle.
Changing packaging colours on an existing shampoo bottle is classified as relaunch rather than contraction in the marketing-mix framework.
Eliminating a weak product from the portfolio is classified as contraction rather than line extension in the marketing-mix framework.
Low share in a fast-growing market at launch is classified as question mark rather than cash cow in the marketing-mix framework.
tactical_explanations:
Adding yogurts beside ice cream creates a new product line and is mix extension. Line extension would add variants inside the ice-cream line itself. Calling the yogurt addition line extension confuses width expansion with depth expansion. The portfolio gains a second line rather than more ice-cream flavours. The classification in the statement is therefore wrong.

So the statement is False.

Profit usually rises in growth and peaks in maturity. That sales-and-profit path across those stages is the life-cycle pattern the statement reports.

So the statement is True.

Changing packaging colours on an existing shampoo is a relaunch under alteration, not contraction. The product stays; presentation is refreshed.

So the statement is True.

Eliminating a weak product is contraction, not line extension. Line extension would add variants; removal shrinks the range. The statement's classification is correct.

So the statement is True.

Low share in a fast-growing market at launch is a question mark, not a cash cow. Cash cows need high share in low-growth settings instead of that launch profile.

So the statement is True.

title: Poor Dogs Near Decline
context: Review how introductory prices may be set low to attract customers at product launch. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: In the maturity stage, market growth slows while the product may still hold a high market share.
During decline, sales fall and profits fall, sometimes rapidly, as the product nears the end of its life cycle.
The duration of product life cycle stages varies enormously across different product categories.
High share when market growth has slowed is classified as cash cow rather than star in the marketing-mix framework.
Some products such as detergents, toothpaste, or perfumes may have a long or seemingly indefinite maturity phase.
tactical_explanations:
In maturity, market growth slows while the product may still hold high share. Slowing growth with retained strength is the maturity picture the statement gives.

So the statement is True.

During decline, sales fall and profits fall, sometimes quickly, as the product approaches the end of its cycle. Demand weakens and competitive pressure can accelerate the drop. Managers may cut support or prepare elimination when that path continues. The stage is defined by those downward movements, not by peak volume. The statement describes decline correctly.

So the statement is True.

Life-cycle stage lengths vary enormously across product categories. Some mature for decades; others fade within months. That variation is real.

So the statement is True.

High share after market growth has slowed is a cash cow rather than a star. Stars still need high growth alongside high share. The statement's cash-cow reading is right.

So the statement is True.

Detergents, toothpaste, or perfumes may stay in a long or seemingly indefinite maturity phase. Extended maturity for such staples is a classic life-cycle observation.

So the statement is True.

title: Price P and Customer Payments
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: High share while the market is still growing is classified as star rather than poor dog in the marketing-mix framework.
Low share with low market growth near decline is classified as poor dog rather than question mark in the marketing-mix framework.
A low launch price to build market share quickly is classified as penetration pricing rather than price skimming in the marketing-mix framework.
Fad products may have a very short life cycle and be withdrawn in less than a year.
A high initial price later reduced over time is classified as price skimming rather than penetration pricing in the marketing-mix framework.
tactical_explanations:
High share while the market is still growing marks a star, not a poor dog. Poor dogs combine low share with low growth near decline instead.

So the statement is True.

Low share with low market growth near decline is a poor dog, not a question mark. Question marks need high growth despite low share. The classification in the statement matches BCG logic.

So the statement is True.

A low launch price meant to build share quickly is penetration pricing. Price skimming instead starts high and may fall later as competition rises. The two strategies aim at different early revenue and volume goals. Managers choose penetration when rapid trial and share matter more than early skim margins. Labelling the low-launch path as penetration rather than skimming is therefore correct.

So the statement is True.

Fad products may run a very short life cycle and leave the market in less than a year. Brief popularity then withdrawal is the fad pattern named here.

So the statement is True.

A high initial price later reduced over time is price skimming, not penetration. Penetration would start low to chase volume from the outset.

So the statement is True.

title: Introductory Low Pricing at Launch
context: Review penetration pricing as a strategy that sets a low price to gain market share quickly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Increased competition in maturity often causes lower prices and higher promotional costs, pressuring profits.
The Boston Consulting Group matrix classifies products using relative market share and market growth.
A product with low relative market share in a rapidly growing market is classified as a question mark.
During introduction a product can be a question mark with low share in a growing market.
As market share rises in a still-growing market, a product may become a star in the BCG matrix.
tactical_explanations:
In maturity, rising competition often forces lower prices and higher promotional spend, which pressures profits. That squeeze from rivalry is a typical maturity dynamic.

So the statement is True.

The Boston Consulting Group matrix classifies products by relative market share and market growth. Those two axes define the four portfolio boxes.

So the statement is True.

A product with low relative market share in a rapidly growing market is a question mark. The growth opportunity is large, yet the firm's competitive weight is still weak. Heavy investment may be needed if managers want to turn it into a star. Without support, the position can stall despite the growing market. The statement assigns that low-share, high-growth cell correctly.

So the statement is True.

During introduction a product can sit as a question mark: low share in a market that is still growing. Early launch often matches that BCG cell.

So the statement is True.

When share rises while the market keeps growing, the product may become a star. Moving from question mark toward star follows that share gain in growth.

So the statement is True.

title: Cost-Plus Pricing Markup Logic
context: Analyze price skimming as setting a high initial price before lowering it over time. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Stars are valuable because of their strong market position in a growing market.
Businesses invest in promotion and production facilities to maintain a star's strong position.
When market growth slows but market share remains high, a product may become a cash cow.
Cash cows usually receive lower investment because market growth has become low while revenues stay high.
As a product nears decline with low market growth and relatively low share, it increasingly becomes a poor dog.
tactical_explanations:
