Stars are valuable because they hold a strong market position while the market itself is still growing. High relative share plus growth creates both current strength and future potential. Cash generated and competitive standing make the position worth defending. Managers therefore treat stars as priority assets in the portfolio. The statement's value reading matches that BCG logic.

So the statement is True.

Firms invest in promotion and production capacity to keep a star's strong position. Defending growth-market leadership requires ongoing support, not neglect.

So the statement is True.

When growth slows but share stays high, the product may become a cash cow. The move from star toward cash cow follows that growth slowdown with retained strength.

So the statement is True.

Cash cows usually receive lower investment because growth is low while revenues remain high. Harvesting cash with lighter spend is the typical treatment.

So the statement is True.

As a product nears decline with low growth and relatively low share, it increasingly becomes a poor dog. Weak share in a fading market is that BCG corner.

So the statement is True.

title: Penetration Pricing for Market Share
context: Consider a beverage company using charm pricing on supermarket shelves and trade discounts for large retailers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Poor dogs combine low relative market share with low market growth in the BCG framework.
Stars occupy high relative market share combined with high market growth on the BCG matrix.
The price element of the marketing mix refers to the amount customers pay for the goods or services offered.
Affordable price is part of the basic marketing-mix idea alongside convenient place and promotional communication.
Introductory prices may be set low at product launch to attract customers during the introduction phase.
tactical_explanations:
Poor dogs combine low relative market share with low market growth on the BCG matrix. That weak-weak cell is the definition the statement uses.

So the statement is True.

Stars occupy high relative market share together with high market growth. Leadership in an expanding market is what makes the cell a star rather than a cash cow or question mark. Investment aims to protect that dual strength. Losing either share or growth would push the product toward another box. The statement places stars on those two high axes correctly.

So the statement is True.

The price element is the amount customers pay for the goods or services offered. Payment for the offer is the core meaning of that marketing-mix P.

So the statement is True.

An affordable price sits beside convenient place and promotional communication in the basic marketing-mix idea. Price is one of those coordinated pillars.

So the statement is True.

Introductory prices may be set low at launch to attract customers in the introduction phase. Trial-friendly launch pricing is a recognised introduction tactic.

So the statement is True.

title: Price Skimming on New Products
context: Analyze psychological pricing such as charm prices that influence customer perceptions. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs when setting the selling price of a product.
Selling only through the firm's own shops is classified as direct distribution rather than indirect distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler is classified as indirect distribution rather than direct distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Television commercials communicating product benefits is classified as advertising rather than place in the marketing-mix framework.
Penetration pricing sets a relatively low price to gain market share quickly after launch.
tactical_explanations:
Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs to set the selling price. Cost base plus margin is the cost-plus rule the statement states.

So the statement is True.

Selling only through the firm's own shops is direct distribution because no independent intermediary sits between producer and buyer. Own-shop paths illustrate that direct place choice.

So the statement is True.

Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler is indirect distribution: the wholesaler is an intermediary on the path to retail. Direct would skip that middle step.

So the statement is True.

Television commercials that communicate product benefits are advertising under promotion, not place decisions about physical access. Ads persuade and inform; warehouses and aisles handle availability. Mixing the commercial with place would confuse message tools with channel tools. Media spend belongs in the promotion toolkit. The statement's advertising classification is therefore right.

So the statement is True.

Penetration pricing sets a relatively low price to gain market share quickly after launch. Fast volume through a low entry price is the penetration aim.

So the statement is True.

title: Competitive Pricing Against Rivals
context: Review discounts, payment terms, and allowances as tools within the price P. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Price skimming sets a high initial price that may be lowered later as competition increases.
Competitive pricing aligns the product's price with rival offerings in the same market.
Making a product available in supermarket aisles is classified as place rather than promotion in the marketing-mix framework.
Psychological pricing uses prices such as €9.99 to influence customer perceptions of affordability.
Discounts, payment terms, and trade allowances form part of the price tools within the marketing mix.
tactical_explanations:
Price skimming starts with a high initial price that may later fall as competition increases. Early skim then gradual reduction is the skimming path.

So the statement is True.

Competitive pricing sets the product's price in line with rival offerings in the same market. Matching or tracking competitors is the competitive-pricing logic named here.

So the statement is True.

Making a product available in supermarket aisles is a place decision about where customers can buy. Promotion would communicate about the product rather than put it on the shelf. Aisle presence is distribution access, not an advertising tool by itself. Channel coverage and retail listing sit under place for that reason. The statement correctly assigns supermarket availability to place rather than promotion.

So the statement is True.

Psychological pricing uses prices such as €9.99 to shape perceptions of affordability. Charm endings are a classic psychological-pricing device.

So the statement is True.

Discounts, payment terms, and trade allowances are price tools inside the marketing mix. They adjust what buyers effectively pay without changing the core list alone.

So the statement is True.

title: Psychological Charm Pricing
context: Consider a book publisher selling through bookshops, online platforms, and direct school supply contracts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: List price and negotiated trade discounts together shape the effective price paid by channel customers.
Sales representatives visiting business clients is classified as personal selling rather than public relations in the marketing-mix framework.
Price differentiation charges different prices to distinct customer groups or distribution channels.
Press releases building corporate reputation is classified as public relations rather than sales promotion in the marketing-mix framework.
A temporary price reduction during a sales event is a price decision linked to promotional activity.
tactical_explanations:
List price and negotiated trade discounts together determine the effective price channel customers actually pay. A high list with a deep trade cut can land near a lower net than a modest list with no discount. Channel negotiations therefore belong inside price management, not only as paperwork beside it. Effective price is the outcome managers track. The statement links list and trade discounts to that effective price correctly.

So the statement is True.

Sales representatives visiting business clients practise personal selling, not public relations. Direct sales contact is the personal-selling tool; PR builds broader image through other channels.

So the statement is True.

Price differentiation charges different prices to distinct customer groups or channels. Segment- or channel-based price splits are that differentiation tool.

So the statement is True.

Press releases that build corporate reputation are public relations, not sales promotion. Image-building communications sit under PR rather than short-term purchase incentives.

So the statement is True.

A temporary price cut during a sales event is a price decision tied to promotional activity. Event pricing bridges price and promotion without erasing either P.

So the statement is True.

title: Discounts and Payment Terms
context: Review direct distribution where a business sells products without intermediaries to buyers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Finance instalment offers spread customer payments over time as part of the overall price package.
Loyalty discounts reward repeat customers and form part of the price element of the marketing mix.
Losses from development costs before sales take off is classified as introduction rather than maturity in the marketing-mix framework.
The place element of the marketing mix concerns where and how the product is made available to customers.
A convenient place for customers to buy supports the basic marketing-mix objective of accessible purchase.
tactical_explanations:
Finance instalment offers spread payments over time and form part of the overall price package customers face. Timing of payment belongs with price design, not only with product features.

So the statement is True.

Loyalty discounts reward repeat customers and sit inside the price element of the mix. Lower prices for returning buyers adjust what loyal customers pay and encourage repurchase. Those discounts are not advertising messages alone; they change the money exchanged. Retention pricing tools therefore belong under price alongside list and trade terms. The statement places loyalty discounts correctly.

So the statement is True.

Losses from development costs before sales take off belong to introduction, not maturity. Maturity is later, when growth has slowed and profit often peaks.

So the statement is True.

Place concerns where and how the product is made available to customers. Access and distribution channels are the place agenda, not the firm's internal office address alone.

So the statement is True.

A convenient place to buy supports the basic marketing-mix goal of accessible purchase. Easy access is one pillar of that coordinated mix idea.

So the statement is True.

title: Place P and Distribution Channels
context: Analyze indirect distribution through wholesalers and retailers to reach final consumers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Rapid sales increases with falling average costs is classified as growth rather than decline in the marketing-mix framework.
Profit peaking while market growth slows is classified as maturity rather than introduction in the marketing-mix framework.
Falling sales and profits as demand weakens is classified as decline rather than growth in the marketing-mix framework.
Place decisions focus on customer access and distribution channels rather than the firm's own office location.
Direct distribution sells products to customers without using intermediaries such as wholesalers or retailers.
tactical_explanations:
Rapid sales increases with falling average costs mark growth rather than decline. Decline shows falling sales, not accelerating volume with better costs.

So the statement is True.

Profit peaking while market growth slows marks maturity rather than introduction. Introduction is early and often loss-making; maturity is where profit commonly peaks.

So the statement is True.

Falling sales and profits as demand weakens mark decline rather than growth. Growth is the rising-sales phase; decline is the opposite trajectory. Managers may cut support or prepare exit when that weakening continues. Confusing decline with growth would reverse the life-cycle reading entirely. The statement assigns the falling path to decline correctly.

So the statement is True.

Place decisions focus on customer access and distribution channels, not on where the firm's own offices sit. Buyer reach matters more than headquarters location for this P.

So the statement is True.

Direct distribution sells to customers without wholesalers or retailers in between. Skipping intermediaries is the defining feature of that place choice.

So the statement is True.

title: Direct Distribution Without Intermediaries
context: Consider a furniture retailer combining showroom display, home-delivery logistics, and finance instalment offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Indirect distribution uses intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers to reach final consumers.
Wholesalers purchase products in bulk and resell them to retailers within a distribution channel.
Retailers make products available to end customers at shops, supermarkets, or other points of sale.
Online sales platforms can serve as a place channel alongside physical shops for the same product.
Selling through own shops is an example of direct distribution within the place element of the mix.
tactical_explanations:
Indirect distribution uses intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers to reach final consumers. Middlemen on the path are what make the channel indirect.

So the statement is True.

Wholesalers buy in bulk and resell to retailers inside the distribution channel. Bulk-in, retail-out is the classic wholesaler role described here.

So the statement is True.

Retailers make products available to end customers at shops, supermarkets, or other points of sale. They sit at the last commercial step before the household or final buyer. Without retail access, many consumer goods would not reach everyday purchase occasions. Place planning therefore treats retailers as a core intermediary type. The statement describes that end-customer access role correctly.

So the statement is True.

Online sales platforms can serve as a place channel alongside physical shops for the same product. Digital and physical access can coexist under place.

So the statement is True.

Selling through own shops is direct distribution within the place element. The firm reaches buyers without independent intermediaries on that path.

So the statement is True.

title: Indirect Distribution Through Retailers
context: Analyze how retailers make products available to end customers at the point of purchase. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler illustrates indirect distribution in the place P.
Intensive distribution places products in many outlets to maximise convenience for customers.
Selective distribution limits the number of outlets to protect brand positioning and service standards.
Exclusive distribution uses a very limited number of specialised partners to sell the product.
Home-delivery logistics extend place convenience after a customer purchases from a showroom.
tactical_explanations:
Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler illustrates indirect distribution in the place P. The wholesaler stands between producer and retail outlet, so the path is not direct. Indirect channels trade some control for broader retail reach. Managers accept that middle step when supermarket coverage matters. The statement's illustration matches the indirect pattern.

So the statement is True.

Intensive distribution places products in many outlets to maximise convenience. Wide availability is the intensive coverage goal for customers.

So the statement is True.

Selective distribution limits outlet numbers to protect brand positioning and service standards. Fewer, chosen partners keep control higher than intensive coverage.

So the statement is True.

Exclusive distribution uses a very limited set of specialised partners. Scarcity of outlets supports premium positioning and tight partner standards.

So the statement is True.

Home-delivery logistics extend place convenience after a showroom purchase. Delivery continues the access promise beyond the store floor itself.

So the statement is True.

title: Wholesaler Role in Distribution
context: Review online sales channels as part of place decisions alongside physical outlets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Distribution channel analysis can reveal weaknesses and encourage alternative channels in place planning.
The promotion element of the marketing mix covers communicating a message in order to promote the sale of the product.
Advertising informs and persuades target customers as a promotional tool within the marketing mix.
Because breakfast cereals are physical goods, services such as installation or support cannot be counted in the product P for that business.
A global breakfast cereals brand guarantees that product quality may vary sharply between countries without affecting brand recognition.
tactical_explanations:
Distribution-channel analysis can reveal weaknesses and push managers toward alternative channels in place planning. Spotting gaps is meant to trigger channel remedies.

So the statement is True.

Promotion covers communicating a message in order to promote the sale of the product. Advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and public relations sit under that communication umbrella. Without a message path, customers may never learn why they should buy. Place puts the product within reach; promotion explains and persuades. The statement defines that promotional role correctly.

So the statement is True.

Advertising informs and persuades target customers as a promotional tool. Information plus persuasion is the advertising job inside the mix.

So the statement is True.

Even when breakfast cereals are physical goods, installation or support services can still count under the product P for that business. Services remain products when offered.

So the statement is False.

A global brand typically signals consistent quality to protect recognition; sharp quality swings across countries would undermine that recognition. Guaranteeing wild quality variation without harm to recognition contradicts brand logic.

So the statement is False.

title: Retailer Access for Final Customers
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Selling breakfast cereals exclusively through wholesalers means the business uses direct distribution with no intermediaries.
Sales promotion includes short-term incentives and sales events designed to stimulate purchase.
Personal selling involves direct contact between sales staff and customers to promote the product.
Public relations activities build a favourable image of the business or brand among stakeholders.
Setting a low introductory price for new breakfast cereals is an example of price skimming aimed only at early luxury buyers.
tactical_explanations:
Selling exclusively through wholesalers means intermediaries are used, so distribution is indirect. Direct distribution would skip wholesalers entirely.

So the statement is False.

Sales promotion uses short-term incentives and sales events to stimulate purchase. Temporary push tools sit under that promotional category.

So the statement is True.

Personal selling involves direct contact between sales staff and customers to promote the product. Face-to-face or direct sales dialogue is the personal-selling path.

So the statement is True.

Public relations builds a favourable image of the business or brand among stakeholders. Press work, community messages, and reputation management belong here rather than in short-term coupon events alone. Image effects can support sales indirectly by raising trust. Managers use PR when credibility and standing matter alongside harder sell tools. The statement places PR in that image-building role correctly.

So the statement is True.

A low introductory price to win early volume is penetration pricing. Price skimming aims high at early luxury or early-adopter willingness to pay, not low launch pricing.

So the statement is False.

title: Online and Physical Place Channels
context: Review the promotion element of the marketing mix as communicating a message to promote sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Removing an outdated breakfast cereals model after failed relaunch attempts is an example of product-mix expansion through mix extension.
Businesses may spend heavily on promotion through advertisements and sales events during product introduction.
A breakfast cereals product with high market share in a no-growth market is a question mark requiring maximum market-growth investment.
Promotional spending in the growth stage helps maintain a star product's strong market position.
Cash-cow products in low-growth markets usually receive lower promotional investment than stars.
tactical_explanations:
Removing an outdated model after failed relaunches is contraction, not mix extension. Mix extension would add a new product line rather than cut an old one.

So the statement is False.

Firms may spend heavily on advertisements and sales events during introduction to create awareness and trial. Heavy early promotion is a common introduction pattern.

So the statement is True.

High share in a no-growth market is a cash cow, not a question mark. Question marks have low share in high-growth markets and may need growth investment. Treating a high-share, no-growth cereal as a question mark that needs maximum growth spend reverses BCG placement. Cash cows are usually harvested with lighter investment. The statement therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Promotional spending in growth helps maintain a star's strong market position. Stars still need that continued support while the market expands.

So the statement is True.

Cash-cow products in low-growth markets usually receive lower promotional investment than stars. Harvesting with lighter spend fits that low-growth, high-share cell.

So the statement is True.

title: Customer Access Not Firm Location
context: Analyze advertising as a promotional tool that informs and persuades target customers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Window displays and social-media campaigns are promotional tools communicating the product message.
Brochure advertising and reservation campaigns can coordinate promotion with price and place decisions.
A sales force calling on business customers is part of the promotion mix for organisational buyers.
Promotional messages should reflect the needs of the targeted segment identified through market research.
Increased competition near decline may raise promotional costs as firms fight for remaining demand.
tactical_explanations:
Window displays and social-media campaigns communicate the product message and therefore count as promotional tools. Both push information and persuasion toward target buyers. Place would be about where the product can be obtained; these tools talk about the offer. Managers mix offline and online message channels under promotion for that reason. The statement classifies those displays and campaigns correctly.

So the statement is True.

Brochure advertising and reservation campaigns can coordinate promotion with price and place decisions. Message, offer terms, and access timing work best when planned together.

So the statement is True.

A sales force calling on business customers is part of the promotion mix for organisational buyers. Personal selling carries the promotional contact in that B2B setting.

So the statement is True.

Promotional messages should reflect the needs of the targeted segment identified through market research. Research-based fit keeps claims relevant to the intended audience.

So the statement is True.

Near decline, rising competition may push promotional costs up as firms fight for remaining demand. Higher spend on a shrinking market is a recognised late-cycle pressure.

So the statement is True.

title: Promotion P and Communicating Messages
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market research findings inform product design, pricing levels, distribution channels, and promotional messages together.
A harmonised marketing mix aligns affordable price, convenient place, suitable product, and clear promotional message.
Promoting breakfast cereals through social-media posts is a place decision because it chooses the warehouse where stock is stored.
Charm pricing of breakfast cereals at €9.99 is a promotional message and not part of the price element of the marketing mix.
Because running shoes are physical goods, services such as installation or support cannot be counted in the product P for that business.
tactical_explanations:
Market research informs product design, pricing, distribution channels, and promotional messages together. All four Ps draw on findings about the target market.

So the statement is True.

A harmonised marketing mix aligns an affordable price, a convenient place, a suitable product, and a clear promotional message. Each P supports the same customer target rather than pulling in conflicting directions. Research findings feed that alignment so the offer, charge, access path, and message fit one another. Without harmony, a strong ad can promise what place cannot deliver. The statement captures that coordinated mix idea correctly.

So the statement is True.

Social-media posts that promote cereals are promotion, not place. Place chooses how and where buyers obtain the product, not which warehouse holds stock for an ad post.

So the statement is False.

Charm pricing at €9.99 is a price-element tool that shapes payment perceptions. It is not merely a promotional slogan outside price. Psychological price endings belong under price.

So the statement is False.

Running shoes being physical goods does not block services such as fitting support from counting under the product P. Offered services remain products in the mix.

So the statement is False.

title: Advertising as Promotional Tool
context: Analyze personal selling as direct promotional contact between sales staff and customers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A global running shoes brand guarantees that product quality may vary sharply between countries without affecting brand recognition.
Selling running shoes exclusively through wholesalers means the business uses direct distribution with no intermediaries.
Setting a low introductory price for new running shoes is an example of price skimming aimed only at early luxury buyers.
Different business units may offer products with distinct characteristics and cycles that address separate customer segments.
Removing an outdated running shoes model after failed relaunch attempts is an example of product-mix expansion through mix extension.
tactical_explanations:
Global brands usually protect recognition by keeping quality reasonably consistent across countries. Sharp quality swings would damage recognition, not leave it untouched.

So the statement is False.

Exclusive selling through wholesalers uses intermediaries and is therefore indirect distribution. Direct distribution would reach buyers without that wholesale middle step.

So the statement is False.

A low introductory price aimed at building volume is penetration pricing. Price skimming sets a high early price for buyers willing to pay more at launch. Treating a low launch price as skimming aimed only at luxury early adopters reverses both the level and the usual skimming audience. Penetration seeks quick share; skimming seeks early margin. The statement therefore mislabels the tactic.

So the statement is False.

Different business units may offer products with distinct characteristics and cycles aimed at separate segments. Portfolio diversity across units is a normal organisational pattern.

So the statement is True.

Removing an outdated model after failed relaunches is contraction, not mix extension. Expansion would add lines or deepen lines rather than eliminate a weak model.

So the statement is False.

title: Sales Promotion and Sales Events
context: Review public relations as promotion that builds a favourable image of the business or brand. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Used equipment sales, support services, and tailored software can coexist as distinct products in one portfolio.
Adding a new flavour variant within an existing household cleaners range is a line extension that deepens the product line.
Introducing an entirely new household cleaners product line alongside an existing range is a mix extension widening the portfolio.
A running shoes product with high market share in a no-growth market is a question mark requiring maximum market-growth investment.
Refreshing household cleaners packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
tactical_explanations:
Used equipment sales, support services, and tailored software can coexist as distinct products in one portfolio. Multiple offer types under one firm fit the product element.

So the statement is True.

Adding a new flavour inside an existing household-cleaners range is line extension that deepens that line. Depth rises without creating a separate line.

So the statement is True.

Introducing an entirely new household-cleaners product line beside an existing range is mix extension that widens the portfolio. Width grows because a distinct line appears, not merely another variant of the old line. Managers use mix extension when they want new categories under the same business. Confusing that move with line extension would understate how much the mix changes. The statement classifies the new-line addition correctly.

So the statement is True.

High share in a no-growth market is a cash cow, not a question mark needing maximum growth investment. Question marks have low share in high-growth markets.

So the statement is False.

Refreshing household-cleaners packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch under product-mix alteration. Presentation changes while the product stays.

So the statement is True.

title: Personal Selling to Customers
context: Consider a beverage company using charm pricing on supermarket shelves and trade discounts for large retailers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Removing an underperforming household cleaners variant from the range reflects contraction in the product-mix strategy.
A household cleaners brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition in the product P.
Low introductory pricing for a new household cleaners product can attract first buyers during the introduction life-cycle stage.
Selling household cleaners through both a company website and partner retailers combines online and indirect place channels.
Seasonal sales events promoting household cleaners are sales-promotion tools within the promotion element of the mix.
tactical_explanations:
Removing an underperforming household-cleaners variant is contraction in the product-mix strategy. The range shrinks when weak items leave. Contraction differs from relaunch, which would try a refresh first, and from extension, which would add offerings. Managers prune when support no longer pays off. The statement places that removal under contraction correctly.

So the statement is True.

A brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition under the product P. Visible brand cues help buyers tell the offer apart.

So the statement is True.

Low introductory pricing for a new household-cleaners product can attract first buyers in the introduction stage. Trial-friendly launch prices fit that early life-cycle phase.

So the statement is True.

Selling through a company website and partner retailers combines online and indirect place channels. Digital direct access and retail intermediaries can run together.

So the statement is True.

Seasonal sales events promoting household cleaners are sales-promotion tools within promotion. Short-term purchase incentives and events sit in that promotional category.

So the statement is True.

title: Public Relations and Brand Image
context: Review how promotion in the growth stage supports maintaining a star's market position. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Promoting running shoes through social-media posts is a place decision because it chooses the warehouse where stock is stored.
Charm pricing of running shoes at €9.99 is treated only as advertising copy and never as a price decision.
Because smart watches are physical goods, services such as installation or support cannot be counted in the product P for that business.
Adding a new flavour variant within an existing sportswear range is a line extension that deepens the product line.
Introducing an entirely new sportswear product line alongside an existing range is a mix extension widening the portfolio.
tactical_explanations:
Social-media posts promoting running shoes are promotion, not place. Place concerns access and distribution, not which warehouse an ad references.

So the statement is False.

Charm pricing at €9.99 is a price decision that shapes what customers pay and how affordable the figure feels. Treating it only as advertising copy and never as price ignores the psychological-pricing tool inside the price P. Message may mention the figure, yet the ending itself is a pricing choice. Price and promotion can interact without erasing the price classification. The statement's never-a-price reading is therefore false.

So the statement is False.

Smart watches being physical goods does not prevent installation or support services from counting under the product P. Services offered with or beside the watch remain products.

So the statement is False.

Adding a new flavour variant within an existing sportswear range is line extension that deepens the line. Depth increases inside the same line identity.

So the statement is True.

Introducing an entirely new sportswear product line beside an existing range is mix extension that widens the portfolio. A new line raises mix width rather than only line depth.

So the statement is True.

title: Heavy Promotion in Introduction
context: Analyze how reduced promotion spending may accompany cash-cow products in low-growth markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Refreshing sportswear packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
Removing an underperforming sportswear variant from the range reflects contraction in the product-mix strategy.
A sportswear brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition in the product P.
A global smart watches brand guarantees that product quality may vary sharply between countries without affecting brand recognition.
Selling smart watches exclusively through wholesalers means the business uses direct distribution with no intermediaries.
tactical_explanations:
Refreshing sportswear packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch under product-mix alteration. Surface refresh without formula change fits that relaunch path.

So the statement is True.

Removing an underperforming sportswear variant is contraction in the product-mix strategy. Cutting the weak item shrinks the range rather than extending it.

So the statement is True.

A sportswear brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition in the product P. Brand marks help customers identify and prefer the offer.

So the statement is True.

A global smart-watches brand typically protects recognition by keeping quality reasonably stable across markets. Guaranteeing sharp quality swings while claiming recognition is unharmed contradicts how brands work. Travellers and multi-market buyers expect the mark to mean a maintained standard. Undermining quality would erode that expectation. The statement's guarantee of harmless variation therefore fails.

So the statement is False.

Selling smart watches only through wholesalers uses intermediaries and is indirect distribution. Direct distribution would omit those wholesale intermediaries.

So the statement is False.

title: Promotion Investment for Stars
context: Consider a book publisher selling through bookshops, online platforms, and direct school supply contracts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Low introductory pricing for a new sportswear product can attract first buyers during the introduction life-cycle stage.
Selling sportswear through both a company website and partner retailers combines online and indirect place channels.
Seasonal sales events promoting sportswear are sales-promotion tools within the promotion element of the mix.
Adding a new flavour variant within an existing organic cereals range is a line extension that deepens the product line.
Introducing an entirely new organic cereals product line alongside an existing range is a mix extension widening the portfolio.
tactical_explanations:
Low introductory pricing for a new sportswear product can attract first buyers during introduction. Early trial pricing fits that life-cycle stage's need for awareness and trial.

So the statement is True.

Selling sportswear through a company website and partner retailers combines online and indirect place channels. Own-site access and retail partners can operate side by side.

So the statement is True.

Seasonal sales events promoting sportswear are sales-promotion tools within the promotion element. They create short-term reasons to buy through events and incentives rather than only through long-running brand ads. Managers time those pushes to seasons when demand can be stimulated. Sales promotion sits beside advertising, personal selling, and public relations in the promotion mix. The statement places seasonal events in that sales-promotion slot correctly.

So the statement is True.

Adding a new flavour variant within an existing organic-cereals range is line extension that deepens the line. Extra variants raise depth inside the same line.

So the statement is True.

Introducing an entirely new organic-cereals product line beside an existing range is mix extension that widens the portfolio. Portfolio width grows with that new line.

So the statement is True.

title: Reduced Promotion for Cash Cows
context: Analyze how market research underpins decisions across all four Ps of the marketing mix. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Refreshing organic cereals packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
Removing an underperforming organic cereals variant from the range reflects contraction in the product-mix strategy.
Setting a low introductory price for new smart watches is an example of price skimming aimed only at early luxury buyers.
A organic cereals brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition in the product P.
Low introductory pricing for a new organic cereals product can attract first buyers during the introduction life-cycle stage.
tactical_explanations:
Colour refreshes on organic cereals packaging leave the core formula untouched. That kind of surface update is a relaunch inside product-mix alteration, not a new line. Shoppers still meet the same product under a brighter look.

So the statement is True.

Contraction is the deliberate removal of products or lines that no longer earn their place. Taking an underperforming organic cereals variant out of the range is exactly that pruning move. The mix becomes narrower or shallower after the cut. Spelling out the category, the counterexample, and the mix element together keeps the verdict tied to this wording rather than to a neighbouring idea.

So the statement is True.

Introductory pricing that starts low for new smart watches is built to attract first-wave volume, not to skim luxury demand. Skimming would charge high at first and cut later. The statement swaps those strategies and invents a luxury-only aim that low entry pricing does not pursue.

So the statement is False.

An organic cereals brand symbol that repeats on labels builds recognition. Differentiation follows when the mark stays consistent. Those brand elements are product-P choices, not afterthoughts outside the mix.

So the statement is True.

New organic cereals in introduction compete for attention with little track record. Low introductory pricing is one standard way to attract those first customers. The statement's life-cycle reading is right.

So the statement is True.

title: Affordable Price and Convenient Place
context: Review how product-mix contraction eliminates products or lines when relaunch seems unpromising. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Selling organic cereals through both a company website and partner retailers combines online and indirect place channels.
Seasonal sales events promoting organic cereals are sales-promotion tools within the promotion element of the mix.
Removing an outdated smart watches model after failed relaunch attempts is an example of product-mix expansion through mix extension.
Adding a new flavour variant within an existing office stationery range is a line extension that deepens the product line.
Introducing an entirely new office stationery product line alongside an existing range is a mix extension widening the portfolio.
tactical_explanations:
Distribution of organic cereals need not pick only one mode. Website sales plus partner retail cover online and indirect lanes at once. That dual setup matches the place reading in the claim.

So the statement is True.

Promotion-mix language treats seasonal sales events as sales promotion. When those events promote organic cereals, they remain inside the promotion element. The claim's classification is standard.

So the statement is True.

Elimination of an outdated smart watches model after failed relaunch attempts is the opposite of mix extension. Mix extension would introduce another line. The expansion claim should be rejected.

So the statement is False.

A new flavour variant inside an existing office stationery range deepens that line. Line extension adds depth without opening a wholly separate product line. The mix width stays the same while the line grows thicker. Spelling out the category, the counterexample, and the mix element together keeps the verdict tied to this wording rather than to a neighbouring idea.

So the statement is True.

Mix extension adds a new line to the assortment. Launching a fresh office stationery line alongside what already sells widens mix width. The statement names that widening correctly.

So the statement is True.

title: Market Research Across Four Ps
context: Consider a furniture retailer combining showroom display, home-delivery logistics, and finance instalment offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A smart watches product with high market share in a no-growth market is a question mark requiring maximum market-growth investment.
Refreshing office stationery packaging colours without changing the core formula is a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
Promoting smart watches through social-media posts is a place decision because it chooses the warehouse where stock is stored.
Removing an underperforming office stationery variant from the range reflects contraction in the product-mix strategy.
Listing smart watches at €9.99 means the firm has left the price element unused and relied only on promotion.
tactical_explanations:
Cash cows hold strong share when the market has little growth left; they fund other units rather than demand maximum growth spend. Question marks sit in high-growth cells with weak share and may need investment to chase leadership. Labelling a high-share, no-growth smart watches product a question mark reverses that map. The required "maximum market-growth investment" story belongs elsewhere, if anywhere.

So the statement is False.

A packaging-colour refresh for office stationery does not rewrite the underlying formula. Product-mix alteration treats that cosmetic change as a relaunch of the same item. Depth and width of the mix stay put while appearance is renewed.

So the statement is True.

Digital promotion of smart watches through social posts does not become place merely because goods sit in warehouses somewhere. Message channel and stock location remain distinct mix decisions.

So the statement is False.

Product-mix strategy allows managers to delete lines or variants that drag results. Removing a weak office stationery option is contraction, not a relaunch and not a line extension. The statement's label matches that elimination logic.

So the statement is True.

Listings at €9.99 for smart watches set the selling price using psychological pricing. That is not abandoning the price P for promotion alone. The statement misplaces the tool.

So the statement is False.

title: Product Elimination After Failed Relaunch
context: Review how increased competition in maturity can lower prices and raise promotional costs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Because energy drinks are physical goods, services such as installation or support cannot be counted in the product P for that business.
A global energy drinks brand guarantees that product quality may vary sharply between countries without affecting brand recognition.
Selling energy drinks exclusively through wholesalers means the business uses direct distribution with no intermediaries.
Setting a low introductory price for new energy drinks is an example of price skimming aimed only at early luxury buyers.
A office stationery brand symbol and consistent label design support differentiation and recognition in the product P.
tactical_explanations:
Services such as installation sit inside the product P even for tangible energy drinks. The product is the whole exchange package, not only the physical unit. The claim should be rejected.

So the statement is False.

Global brands for energy drinks usually protect recognition by keeping quality cues consistent across countries. Sharp quality swings without harming recognition contradict that logic. The statement's "guarantee" of harmless variation is false. Spelling out the category, the counterexample, and the mix element together keeps the verdict tied to this wording rather than to a neighbouring idea.

So the statement is False.

Wholesalers sit between producer and many retailers or buyers. Exclusive wholesale selling of energy drinks is therefore indirect, not direct. The statement's direct-distribution label is inverted.

So the statement is False.

Introductory pricing that starts low for new energy drinks is built to attract first-wave volume, not to skim luxury demand. Skimming would charge high at first and cut later. The statement swaps those strategies and invents a luxury-only aim that low entry pricing does not pursue.

So the statement is False.

An office stationery brand symbol that repeats on labels builds recognition. Differentiation follows when the mark stays consistent. Those brand elements are product-P choices, not afterthoughts outside the mix.

So the statement is True.

title: Economies of Scale in Growth
context: Analyze how a fad product may have a very short life cycle withdrawn in under a year. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Low introductory pricing for a new office stationery product can attract first buyers during the introduction life-cycle stage.
Removing an outdated energy drinks model after failed relaunch attempts is an example of product-mix expansion through mix extension.
A energy drinks product with high market share in a no-growth market is a question mark requiring maximum market-growth investment.
Promoting energy drinks through social-media posts is a place decision because it chooses the warehouse where stock is stored.
A €9.99 charm price for energy drinks is classified exclusively under promotion rather than the price mix element.
tactical_explanations:
New office stationery in introduction compete for attention with little track record. Low introductory pricing is one standard way to attract those first customers. The statement's life-cycle reading is right.

So the statement is True.

Product-mix expansion would deepen or widen what is sold. Removing a dated energy drinks model after failed relaunch does neither. The statement's expansion framing is false.

So the statement is False.

Maximum growth investment is aimed at building question marks or defending stars, not at labelling a high-share stagnant energy drinks item a question mark. The statement mismatches category and prescription.

So the statement is False.

Social-media promotion of energy drinks belongs with advertising and digital campaigns in the promotion element. It does not choose warehouse sites. The place classification in the statement is wrong.

So the statement is False.

A €9.99 tag on energy drinks is psychological or charm pricing inside the price P. It may appear in ads, yet the decision itself is a price-element choice. Calling it exclusively promotion leaves price unused in name only. Spelling out the category, the counterexample, and the mix element together keeps the verdict tied to this wording rather than to a neighbouring idea.

title: Price Differentiation Across Groups
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
